name: The Ludb household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: ludb_john

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of 1 July 1834 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). The earliest issue this project reads the name in is 1834-07-02, 1 day later; that gap is an accident of which impression an extraction pass reached, and it is not evidence. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1834-07-01 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

lives_at.note: Not attested: a letter list gives a name and no address.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded, so there is no premises to seek.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Nothing after 1834-07-16 follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

occupation.note: No source records an occupation for this person. A list of uncalled-for letters prints a name and no trade, and this pass will not read one in.

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'John Ludb' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 2 July 1834, column 29, reprinted over 3 consecutive issues — dated 1834-07-02 to 1834-07-16. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

merge_ruling.for_merge: A terminal y lost, 'John' identical, and 'Ludb' is set NOWHERE in the deposited corpus while Ludby is set three times — the profile of a truncated reading rather than a family. John Ludby is a documented man: Fergus 1843 has 'Ludby, John, soap and candle maker, South Branch, 3 miles south [died January 24, 1872, aged 78.]', and the Democrat prints him on 19 November 1834.
merge_ruling.against_merge: THE TWO INSTRUMENTS NEVER TOUCH. 'John Ludb' is the post-office return of 2 July 1834 (#c029) and nothing else; John Ludby is the Democrat of 19 November 1834 (#c006) and Fergus 1843 — a letter list against a newspaper and a directory, D7's own example. No issue and no return is caught setting both spellings, and the letter-list card is not an anchor: T-0482 closed it no_corroboration. The fold is admissible in shape and has no demonstration behind it, which is exactly what D7 is for. `for_merge` is kept because a later reading of the 2 July 1834 return's image could show the terminal y in the impression and close this.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
